description: AutoCAD Express Tools not covered in the other chunks: attribute import, block trimming, hyperlink editing, dimension-style import, editing-time tracking, Julian date routines, Drawing Properties population, linetype and shape makers, HPGL import, paper-space text scaling, leader attachment, path redirection, file/session utilities (REVERT, SAVEALL, QQUIT), remote-text editing, dynamic UCS rotation, text enclosures and justification, frame toggles, viewport scale reporting and XData tools. Express Tools are installed with AutoCAD for Windows (not LT, Mac or web) and loaded by EXPRESSTOOLS.

tools.name: ATTIN
tools.description: Imports block attribute values from a tab-delimited text file, usually one created by ATTOUT and edited in a spreadsheet. Rows are matched to block references by the HANDLE column, so values are written back to exactly the blocks they came from.
tools.usage:
ATTIN  (Express > Blocks > Import Attribute Information)
select the .txt file in the file dialog

parameters.name: HANDLE column
parameters.description: First column; identifies the block reference. Do not edit it.

parameters.name: BLOCKNAME column
parameters.description: Informational; the block itself is found by handle.

parameters.name: tag columns
parameters.description: One column per attribute tag; edited values are written back.

tools.example:
1. ATTOUT -> select title blocks -> C:\Temp\titles.txt
2. Edit REV and DATE columns in Excel, save as tab-delimited text
3. ATTIN -> C:\Temp\titles.txt
tools.notes: Handles are drawing-specific, so the file only works for the drawing it was exported from. Keep the file tab-delimited (Excel 'Text (Tab delimited)'); CSV will not import.

tools.name: BTRIM
tools.description: Trims objects to cutting edges that are nested inside block references or xrefs, which the standard TRIM cannot select directly. Its companion BEXTEND extends objects to nested edges.
tools.usage:
BTRIM
Select cutting edges (block references or xrefs, then pick nested objects)
Select object to trim

parameters.name: cutting edges
parameters.description: Objects inside blocks or xrefs picked as edges.

parameters.name: Shift-select
parameters.description: Holding Shift extends instead of trimming, as in TRIM.

tools.example:
BTRIM
<pick wall lines inside the xref as cutting edges>
<Enter>
<pick the ends of the hatch boundary lines to trim>
tools.notes: Since AutoCAD 2021 TRIM/EXTEND Quick mode can use nested geometry in many cases; BTRIM remains useful for precise edge selection inside blocks.

tools.name: CHURLS
tools.description: Edits the URL (hyperlink address) attached to a selected object one object at a time, showing the current address for modification.
tools.usage:
CHURLS
Select object with URL
Enter new URL

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: An object that already has a hyperlink (HYPERLINK command).

tools.notes: Use REPURLS to replace a text string in many hyperlinks at once and SHOWURLS to review all hyperlinks.

tools.name: DIMIM
tools.description: Imports named dimension styles and their settings from a .dim file created by DIMEX, optionally overwriting existing styles of the same name. Together with DIMEX it transfers dimension standards between drawings without copying geometry.
tools.usage: DIMIM  (dialog: Import Filename + Import Options)

parameters.name: Import Filename
parameters.description: ASCII .dim file in the format written by DIMEX.

parameters.name: Keep the Existing Style / Overwrite Existing Style
parameters.description: Whether styles already present in the drawing are preserved or replaced.

tools.example:
DIMIM
Import Filename: C:\CAD\Standards\ACME-dims.dim
Import Options: Overwrite Existing Style > OK
tools.notes: Not all current dimension variables are supported by DIMEX/DIMIM, so verify imported styles. DesignCenter or a DWS/template are alternatives for complete style transfer.

tools.name: EDITTIME
tools.description: Tracks the active editing time spent in a drawing, pausing automatically after a configurable period of inactivity. The accumulated time is stored per drawing in the named object dictionary, which makes it usable for simple time reporting.
tools.usage:
EDITTIME
Enter an option [ON/OFF/Reset/Timeout]

parameters.name: ON / OFF
parameters.description: Start/resume or stop the timer.

parameters.name: Reset
parameters.description: Clear the elapsed time to zero.

parameters.name: Timeout
parameters.description: Minutes of inactivity after which timing pauses.

tools.notes: Implemented in edittime.arx, which exports acet-edittime-enable, acet-edittime-reset, acet-edittime-total and acet-edittime-timeout for LISP; the total is a Julian-style real in days.

tools.name: EXPLAN
tools.description: Displays a plan view of the XY plane of a specified UCS (current, named or World) without changing the magnification, unlike PLAN which zooms to extents.
tools.usage:
EXPLAN
(options identical to PLAN: Current ucs / Ucs / World)

parameters.name: Current ucs / Ucs / World
parameters.description: Which coordinate system's plan view to show, as in PLAN.

tools.notes: Useful in large drawings where a zoom-extents regen after PLAN is slow.

tools.name: EXPRESSMENU
tools.description: Loads the Express Tools menu and displays the Express menu on the classic menu bar. Useful when the menu bar is on (MENUBAR = 1) but the Express menu is missing.
tools.usage: EXPRESSMENU

parameters.name: MENUBAR
parameters.description: Must be 1 to see pull-down menus.

tools.notes: The ribbon Express Tools tab comes from the acetmain partial CUIx; EXPRESSTOOLS reloads everything if the tab is missing.

tools.name: EXPRESSTOOLS
tools.description: Loads the Express Tools libraries, adds the Express folder to the support search path and loads the Express menu and ribbon tab. Run it when Express commands are reported as unknown after a profile reset or custom deployment.
tools.usage: EXPRESSTOOLS

parameters.name: installation
parameters.description: Express Tools must be selected during AutoCAD installation; otherwise modify the installation to add them.

tools.notes: Express Tools are not available in AutoCAD LT, AutoCAD for Mac or the web app.

tools.name: IMAGEAPP
tools.description: Specifies the external image-editing program that IMAGEEDIT launches for attached raster images, or selects the Windows default application for the file type.
tools.usage:
IMAGEAPP
Image editing application or . for system default: <path to .exe>

parameters.name: application path
parameters.description: Full path of the editor executable; '.' uses the system default.

tools.notes: The setting is stored per user and used by IMAGEEDIT.

tools.name: IMAGEEDIT
tools.description: Opens the source file of a selected raster image in the image editor defined by IMAGEAPP. After saving the edited image, reload it in External References to see the changes.
tools.usage:
IMAGEEDIT
Select image

parameters.name: image
parameters.description: An attached raster image (IMAGEATTACH).

tools.example:
IMAGEEDIT
<select the site photo>
; edit and save in the external editor
-IMAGE
_R
site_photo
tools.notes: Editing the file affects every drawing that references it.

tools.name: JULIAN
tools.description: Express Tools AutoLISP library (julian.lsp) providing the DATE command and date-conversion functions between calendar dates, AutoCAD CDATE-style dates and Julian dates, as used by the DATE and TDCREATE/TDUPDATE system variables.
tools.usage:
(load "julian")
DATE
(ctoj year month day hour minute second) (dtoj yyyymmdd.hhmmss) (jtoc julian) (jtod julian) (jtow julian)

parameters.name: ctoj / dtoj
parameters.description: Calendar values or a CDATE-format real to a Julian date.

parameters.name: jtoc / jtod
parameters.description: Julian date to a calendar list or CDATE format.

parameters.name: jtow
parameters.description: Day of week, 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday.

tools.notes: TDCREATE, TDUPDATE and DATE store Julian day numbers plus fraction of day, so these routines are handy for age or timestamp reports.

tools.name: LSP
tools.description: Lists the AutoLISP commands (c: functions), functions or global variables currently defined in the drawing's LISP namespace, or loads a LISP file. Useful for discovering what a loaded routine provides.
tools.usage:
LSP
Enter an option [Commands/Functions/Variables/Load]

parameters.name: Commands / Functions / Variables
parameters.description: Which group of defined symbols to list.

parameters.name: Load
parameters.description: Load an AutoLISP file.

tools.example:
LSP
C
; lists all C: commands defined by loaded LISP files
tools.notes: For inspecting source files by function, use LSPSURF.

tools.name: LSPSURF
tools.description: Opens an AutoLISP file viewer that displays the file's contents function by function, making it easy to browse unfamiliar LISP files without an external editor.
tools.usage:
LSPSURF
select a .lsp file

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: AutoLISP source file to browse.

tools.notes: Read-only viewer; edit code in Visual Studio Code with the AutoLISP extension or VLIDE.

tools.name: MKLTYPE
tools.description: Creates a linetype definition from drawn geometry (lines, points, shapes and text) and writes it to a .lin file, then loads it. It is the fastest way to build complex linetypes without hand-editing .lin syntax.
tools.usage:
MKLTYPE
Linetype file (.lin) > Linetype name > Description > Starting point > Ending point > Select objects

parameters.name: starting / ending point
parameters.description: Define one repetition length of the pattern.

parameters.name: objects
parameters.description: Lines, points, shapes and text forming the pattern (drawn along X).

tools.example:
MKLTYPE
C:\CAD\Support\acme.lin
FENCE_X
Fence ---x---x---
<pick start> <pick end>
<select the line segments and the X text>
tools.notes: Text in the pattern uses a text style; the style must exist in drawings using the linetype. Draw the sample at 1:1 scale relative to the intended LTSCALE.

tools.name: MKSHAPE
tools.description: Creates a shape definition from selected objects, writes it to an .shp file and compiles it to .shx, so the shape can be used with SHAPE or inside complex linetypes.
tools.usage:
MKSHAPE
Shape file (.shp) > Shape name > Resolution <128> > Insertion base point > Select objects

parameters.name: Resolution
parameters.description: Grid resolution for converting geometry to shape vectors (higher = more accurate).

parameters.name: insertion base point
parameters.description: Origin of the shape.

tools.example:
MKSHAPE
C:\CAD\Support\acme_sym.shp
VALVE
128
0,0
<select the valve symbol geometry>
tools.notes: Shapes are simple vectors (no fills); for rich symbols use blocks instead.

tools.name: PLT2DWG
tools.description: Imports a legacy HPGL plot file (.plt) into the current drawing as geometry, preserving pen colors. Useful to recover drawings that only exist as old plot files.
tools.usage:
PLT2DWG
select the HPGL .plt file

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: HPGL plot file (HPGL/2 files may not convert fully).

tools.notes: Result is plain line work at plotter units; scale it to real units afterwards (SCALE with a known dimension).

tools.name: PROPULATE
tools.description: Populates, lists or removes Drawing Properties (DWGPROPS summary and custom fields) in the current drawing or in all drawings of a folder, using a .prp template. Templates can extract attribute values and lists of xrefs, fonts and images into properties.
tools.usage:
PROPULATE
Enter an option [Update/List/Remove/Active template/Edit template]
then [Current drawing/Other drawings]

parameters.name: Update / List / Remove
parameters.description: Action on the Drawing Properties.

parameters.name: Active template / Edit template
parameters.description: Choose or edit the .prp template (default template.prp).

parameters.name: @[block.attributeTag] / @[XREFLIST] / @[FONTLIST] / @[IMAGELIST]
parameters.description: Template placeholders extracting data from the drawing.

tools.example:
PROPULATE
U
O
<choose folder P:\Proj\Sheets, include subfolders>
tools.notes: Drawing Properties are visible in Windows File Explorer and usable in fields. Custom properties in a template are limited to 10.

tools.name: PSTSCALE
tools.description: Sets or updates the height of text objects in model space so that they plot at a specified paper-space height in a given viewport scale, keeping annotation readable when drawing without annotative scaling.
tools.usage:
PSTSCALE
Select text objects
Specify paper space text height
Specify scale by picking a viewport or [Set/Update]

parameters.name: paper space height
parameters.description: Desired plotted height.

parameters.name: viewport scale
parameters.description: Taken from a picked viewport or entered.

tools.notes: PSBSCALE is the equivalent for blocks. Annotative text (ANNOTATIVE property) is the modern alternative.

tools.name: QLATTACH
tools.description: Attaches an existing leader line to an mtext, tolerance or block reference object so that the annotation and leader become associated.
tools.usage:
QLATTACH
Select leader
Select annotation (mtext, tolerance or block)

parameters.name: leader
parameters.description: A legacy LEADER/QLEADER object.

parameters.name: annotation
parameters.description: Mtext, tolerance or block reference.

tools.example:
QLATTACH
<pick the leader>
<pick the note mtext>
tools.notes: Obsolete since multileaders (MLEADER, MLEADERALIGN, MLEADERCOLLECT, MLEADEREDIT); kept for legacy QLEADER drawings.

tools.name: QLATTACHSET
tools.description: Globally attaches leader lines to the mtext, tolerance or block reference objects they point to, processing a whole selection at once instead of one pair at a time.
tools.usage:
QLATTACHSET
Select objects (leaders and annotations)

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: Leaders and candidate annotations; each leader attaches to the annotation at its end.

tools.notes: Obsolete with multileaders; useful for cleaning up legacy drawings where leaders lost associativity.

tools.name: QLDETACHSET
tools.description: Detaches leader lines from the mtext, tolerance or block reference objects they are associated with, so the annotation can be moved independently.
tools.usage:
QLDETACHSET
Select leaders

parameters.name: leaders
parameters.description: Associated legacy leaders to detach.

tools.notes: Counterpart of QLATTACH/QLATTACHSET; not applicable to MLEADER objects.

tools.name: QQUIT
tools.description: Closes all open drawings and exits AutoCAD in one step, giving the opportunity to save modified drawings as they are closed.
tools.usage: QQUIT

parameters.name: (none)
parameters.description: No options; modified drawings are handled as by CLOSEALL/QUIT.

tools.notes: Run SAVEALL first when every drawing should be saved without individual decisions.

tools.name: REDIR
tools.description: Finds and replaces hard-coded directory paths in xrefs, images, shapes, text styles (font files) and rtext objects, for example after moving a project to another server. Entering * as the old path and nothing as the new one strips all paths so files are found via the support path.
tools.usage:
REDIR
Enter old directory (use '*' for all), or ? for current: 
Replace "<old>" with:

parameters.name: old directory
parameters.description: Path to replace; * for any path, ? to list current paths.

parameters.name: new directory
parameters.description: Replacement path; empty removes the path.

parameters.name: REDIRMODE
parameters.description: Selects which object types REDIR processes.

tools.notes: Does not change rtext or images inside xrefs, or big fonts of xref styles; changes to xref-dependent objects are temporary unless the xref drawings are edited too. For bulk path repair across files, Reference Manager is an alternative.

tools.name: REDIRMODE
tools.description: Sets which object types the REDIR Express Tool processes: styles (fonts and shapes), xrefs, images and rtext. The default is all four.
tools.usage:
REDIRMODE
enter a comma-separated list of the object types to process (default: Styles,Xrefs,Images,Rtext)

parameters.name: Styles
parameters.description: Font and shape files referenced by text styles.

parameters.name: Xrefs / Images / Rtext
parameters.description: Reference paths of external drawings, raster images and remote text.

tools.notes: The setting persists for later REDIR calls in the session.

tools.name: REPURLS
tools.description: Finds and replaces a text string in the hyperlinks (URLs) attached to selected objects, updating many hyperlinks at once after a server or site move.
tools.usage:
REPURLS
Select objects
String to find
Replace with

parameters.name: find / replace strings
parameters.description: Substring replaced in each hyperlink address.

tools.notes: Check results with SHOWURLS.

tools.name: REVERT
tools.description: Closes the current drawing without saving and reopens the last saved version, discarding all changes since the last save after a confirmation.
tools.usage: REVERT

parameters.name: confirmation
parameters.description: Asks whether to abandon changes and reopen.

tools.notes: Unsaved work is lost; UNDO may be a safer way to back out a few steps.

tools.name: RTEDIT
tools.description: Edits existing remote text (RTEXT) objects: their source (an external text file or a DIESEL expression), style, height and rotation.
tools.usage:
RTEDIT
Select rtext object
Options: Style / Height / Rotation / Edit

parameters.name: Edit
parameters.description: Change the file reference or DIESEL expression.

parameters.name: Style / Height / Rotation
parameters.description: Formatting properties.

tools.notes: RTEXT objects need the Express Tools object enabler; in drawings opened without Express Tools they appear as proxies. Fields are the modern alternative.

tools.name: RTUCS
tools.description: Rotates the current UCS dynamically by clicking and dragging about the active axis, with status-line feedback of axis and angle. Options save, restore, delete and cycle named or orthographic UCSs and set the rotation increment, origin, view alignment or World.
tools.usage:
RTUCS
[TAB] change active axis (X/Y/Z)
Options: Save / Restore / Delete / Cycle / Angle / Origin / View / World / Undo

parameters.name: [TAB]
parameters.description: Cycles the active rotation axis X, Y, Z.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Minimum rotation increment for the current axis.

parameters.name: Save / Restore / Delete
parameters.description: Manage named UCSs.

parameters.name: Cycle
parameters.description: Steps through the six standard orthographic UCS orientations.

tools.example:
RTUCS
Angle 15
<TAB to X axis, drag to tilt 30 degrees>
Save ROOF_SLOPE
tools.notes: Handy for 3D sketching on sloped planes; the dynamic UCS (UCSDETECT) often replaces it.

tools.name: SAVEALL
tools.description: Saves all open drawings in one step; unnamed drawings prompt for a file name.
tools.usage: SAVEALL

parameters.name: (none)
parameters.description: No options.

tools.example:
; toolbar macro to save everything and close
^C^CSAVEALL;CLOSEALL;
tools.notes: Read-only drawings cannot be saved and are skipped with a message.

tools.name: SHOWURLS
tools.description: Displays a dialog listing all hyperlinks (URLs) attached to objects in the drawing, with options to show the object and to edit or replace the URLs.
tools.usage: SHOWURLS

parameters.name: Show URL / Edit / Replace
parameters.description: Dialog actions for the selected hyperlink.

tools.example:
SHOWURLS
<select a URL in the list> Show URL
tools.notes: The core HYPERLINK command creates and edits hyperlinks on individual objects.

tools.name: SHP2BLK
tools.description: Replaces all instances of a selected shape object with an equivalent block, creating the block definition from the shape. Useful because shapes depend on SHX files that may be missing on other systems.
tools.usage:
SHP2BLK
Select shape entity to redefine
Enter new block name

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: A SHAPE object whose definition is replaced.

parameters.name: block name
parameters.description: Name for the new block (defaults to the shape name).

tools.notes: All shapes of that name in the drawing are converted.

tools.name: TCIRCLE
tools.description: Encloses each selected text or mtext object with a circle, a slot or a rectangle, with an offset factor relative to text height and either constant (all the size of the largest) or variable sizes.
tools.usage:
TCIRCLE
Select objects
Enter distance offset factor <0.35>
Create Circles, Slots or Rectangles
Create [Constant/Variable] sized ...

parameters.name: offset factor
parameters.description: Gap between text and enclosure as a fraction of text height.

parameters.name: Circles / Slots / Rectangles
parameters.description: Enclosure shape.

parameters.name: Constant / Variable
parameters.description: Same size for all (largest) or sized per text.

tools.notes: Enclosures are separate objects on the current layer; group them with the text or use blocks if they must move together.

tools.name: TEXTUNMASK
tools.description: Removes the masks created by TEXTMASK from selected text or mtext objects, deleting the wipeout, 3D face or solid used as the mask.
tools.usage:
TEXTUNMASK
Select text or mtext objects to unmask

parameters.name: objects
parameters.description: Text previously masked with TEXTMASK.

tools.notes: Masks created with MText background fill are removed through the MText properties, not with TEXTUNMASK.

tools.name: TFRAMES
tools.description: Toggles the display of frames for all wipeout and image objects at once, switching the IMAGEFRAME and WIPEOUTFRAME settings together.
tools.usage: TFRAMES

parameters.name: IMAGEFRAME / WIPEOUTFRAME
parameters.description: System variables controlling frame display and plotting.

tools.example: TFRAMES   ; hide frames before plotting, run again to show them for editing
tools.notes: Frames that are hidden cannot be selected by picking the frame; turn them on to edit clipping boundaries.

tools.name: TJUST
tools.description: Changes the justification point of text objects without moving the text, the Express Tools counterpart of the core JUSTIFYTEXT command.
tools.usage:
TJUST
Select objects
Start/Center/Middle/Right/TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR <current>

parameters.name: justification
parameters.description: New justification; the text keeps its visual position.

tools.notes: Changing justification first makes later alignment operations (e.g. aligning to a grid point) predictable.

tools.name: VPSCALE
tools.description: On a layout, reports the scale of the current viewport or of a picked viewport as a paper-to-model ratio, plus an architectural or engineering scale when those units are active.
tools.usage:
VPSCALE
Select the viewport to list

parameters.name: viewport
parameters.description: Viewport border to check; in an active viewport the current scale is reported without prompting.

tools.notes: Only works in layouts. The core Properties palette and the viewport scale control on the status bar show the same information.

tools.name: XDATA
tools.description: Attaches extended object data (XData) to a selected object interactively, choosing an application name and then entering values of various types. It is a quick way to tag objects for testing LISP or .NET code that reads XData.
tools.usage:
XDATA
Select object
Application name
Data type options: 3Real / Pos / Disp / Dir / Real / Dist / Scale / Int / Long / Hand / Layer / Str (repeat, Enter to finish)

parameters.name: Application name
parameters.description: Registered application name for the XData block (standardise names across projects).

parameters.name: data types
parameters.description: 3 reals, world position/displacement/direction, real, distance, scale, 16-bit int, 32-bit long, handle, layer name, string.

tools.example:
XDATA
<select a pump block>
ACME
Str
PUMP-07
<Enter>
tools.notes: Read it back with XDLIST or (entget e '("ACME")).

tools.name: XDLIST
tools.description: Lists the extended data (XData) attached to a selected object, for one application name or all, showing group codes and values in the text window.
tools.usage:
XDLIST
Select object
Application to list <*>

parameters.name: application
parameters.description: Application name or * for all XData on the object.

tools.notes: Handy for debugging XData written by custom applications.

tools.name: DUMPSHX
tools.description: External Express Tools utility (dumpshx.exe) that converts compiled SHX shape or font files back to SHP source, so shapes can be inspected, fixed or recompiled with COMPILE.
tools.usage: dumpshx.exe [options] file.shx   (run from a Windows command prompt in the Express folder)

parameters.name: file.shx
parameters.description: Compiled shape or font file to decompile.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Run dumpshx without arguments to list the supported switches for output file and format.

tools.notes: Respect font licences; many commercial SHX fonts prohibit decompilation.
